Draft a brief proposal with time-saving estimates and present it when the supervisor returns.

simulation.title: First Morning of Audit Support
simulation.brief: You arrive at the DVAGO head office to start your first day supporting the Internal Audit team. Rank these tasks from FIRST to LAST based on professional priority.

items.t: Meet with your mentor to clarify expectations and access permissions for ERP systems
Review the daily audit schedule and identify any urgent tasks assigned to you
Organize and back up the shared digital audit folder structure
Update your personal to-do list with long-term learning goals
Prepare a draft checklist for the upcoming store visit based on previous templates

simulation.rationale: Prioritizing schedule and mentor alignment ensures you are aligned with immediate team needs and have necessary access before doing operational tasks.

caseStudy.title: Store Inventory Variance
caseStudy.context: DVAGO Store #42 reported a 10% inventory variance in high-value cold chain items during the last month-end count. The store manager claims it is due to supplier delivery errors. However, your preliminary review of the delivery notes shows all goods were signed for as received in full. The total value of the variance is PKR 500,000. The store has a history of minor discrepancies but this is the largest to date.

questions.q: What immediate steps would you take to investigate this variance?

rubric.point: Verify physical count and system records
Review delivery and receipt documentation
Interview store staff and manager
Check CCTV or access logs if available
Escalate findings to supervisor

questions.q: How would you handle the store manager's claim that the supplier is at fault?

rubric.point: Maintain objectivity and neutrality
Request supporting evidence from manager
Compare with supplier records
Document the disagreement clearly
Follow up with supplier if needed

questions.q: What recommendations would you make to prevent similar variances in the future?

rubric.point: Implement dual verification for high-value items
Train staff on proper receiving procedures
Conduct more frequent cycle counts
Review and update SOPs
Monitor key performance indicators

voice.q: Why do you want the Deputy Manager position in Internal Audit at DVAGO and what specific experience makes you suited to it?
Tell me about a time you had to handle a critical audit finding that required immediate escalation to senior management. What was the situation, what did you do, and what was the result?

sjt.title: Audit Team Conflict
sjt.scenario: Two senior auditors on your team disagree on the severity of a DRAP compliance violation found in a high-volume store. The store manager is pressuring them to downgrade the finding to avoid penalties. Your team lead is unavailable.
sjt.question: What is the most effective action?

options.t: Re-evaluate the evidence against SOPs, ensure consistency, and escalate the dispute to the Head of Audit with a clear recommendation.
Ask the auditors to compromise by splitting the severity rating to satisfy both parties.
Support the store manager's request to maintain good relations with the operations team.
Review the evidence against SOPs, confirm the correct severity, and issue a formal warning to the auditors if they resist.

sjt.title: Budget Overrun
sjt.scenario: Your internal audit department is 15% over budget for the quarter due to unexpected travel costs for warehouse audits. The CFO has asked for an explanation and a plan to stay within the annual cap.
sjt.question: What is the most effective action?

options.t: Present a detailed variance analysis and propose shifting high-risk audits to virtual reviews where possible.
Reduce the number of planned audits for the next quarter to save money immediately.
Ignore the overrun for now and hope the next quarter's savings will cover the difference.
Request a budget increase from the CFO citing the importance of thorough compliance checks.

sjt.title: Staff Performance Issue
sjt.scenario: A junior auditor on your team has missed two consecutive deadlines for store audit reports. When asked, they claim the store staff were uncooperative. You know this store is often difficult but the delay is impacting the monthly compliance report.
sjt.question: What is the most effective action?

options.t: Issue a formal warning immediately for failing to meet deadlines.
Coach the auditor on handling difficult stakeholders, set a strict deadline for the next task, and monitor progress closely.
Accept the delay as an external factor and adjust the timeline for the monthly report.
Take over the task yourself to ensure the report is submitted on time.

sjt.title: Data Integrity Check
sjt.scenario: During a surprise audit at a central warehouse, you find that the physical stock count for high-value cold chain items does not match the SAP records. The warehouse supervisor claims a system error occurred.
sjt.question: What is the most effective action?

options.t: Ask the supervisor to correct the records manually and move on to the next audit item.
Accept the supervisor's explanation and note it as a minor system glitch in the report.
Report the discrepancy to the CEO immediately without further investigation.
Freeze the inventory movement for those items and investigate the root cause with IT and operations.

simulation.title: Audit Prioritization
simulation.brief: It is Monday morning. You have four urgent tasks and a team meeting. Rank the following tasks from FIRST to LAST based on risk and impact.

items.t: Review and sign off the critical compliance report due to the Board today.
Address an urgent escalation from a store manager regarding a disputed audit penalty.
Conduct a performance review with a junior auditor who is underperforming.
Prepare the monthly KPI dashboard for the head of audit.
Plan the audit schedule for the next month's warehouse inspections.

simulation.rationale: The Board report is a hard deadline with high visibility, followed by the active escalation which poses immediate operational risk, then people management, then planning, and finally routine reporting.

caseStudy.title: Cold Chain Audit Failure
caseStudy.context: DVAGO is facing a regulatory audit in two weeks. Your team recently conducted a surprise audit at three major stores. You found that 40% of cold chain items (vaccines and insulin) were stored at temperatures above 8°C for more than 4 hours. The store managers claimed they were unaware of the sensor failures. The current cold chain compliance KPI is 95%, and this incident drops it to 82%. The Head of Audit wants a strategy to rectify this before the external auditors arrive. You have a budget of PKR 500,000 for immediate corrective actions.

questions.q: What immediate actions would you take to mitigate the risk for the upcoming regulatory audit?

rubric.point: Immediate verification of remaining stock
Communication with suppliers and pharmacy board
Technical repair of sensors
Staff retraining on SOPs

questions.q: How would you handle the store managers who failed to report the temperature breaches?

rubric.point: Root cause analysis of failure
Disciplinary action vs coaching
Systemic fix for reporting
Impact on KPIs

questions.q: How would you allocate the PKR 500,000 budget for corrective actions?

rubric.point: Prioritizing high-risk items
Investing in technology vs people
Cost-benefit analysis
Documentation of spend

voice.q: Why do you want this specific position at DVAGO and what makes you suited to it? (mention the position)
Tell me about a time you found an error in a record or process. What did you do and what was the result?

sjt.title: Manager Pressure
sjt.scenario: During a store audit, you find that a senior manager has signed off on expense claims for personal purchases. The manager tells you to ignore it to avoid conflict. What is the most effective action?
sjt.question: What is the most effective action?

options.t: Ask the manager to correct the entries quietly without telling anyone else.
Ignore the issue and sign off the audit as complete to maintain good relations.
Confront the manager publicly in the office to ensure everyone knows the truth.
Document the discrepancy with evidence and report it formally to your audit head.

sjt.title: Missing Records
sjt.scenario: You are auditing a warehouse and find that stock records for high-value cold chain products do not match the physical count. The warehouse officer is uncooperative and claims the system is down. What is the most effective action?
sjt.question: What is the most effective action?

options.t: Accept the officer's explanation and note the variance as a temporary system glitch.
Wait for the IT department to fix the system before conducting any further checks.
Perform a recount immediately with a witness and document the actual discrepancy.
Tell the officer that if they do not cooperate, you will file a complaint.

sjt.title: Deadline Rush
sjt.scenario: It is the last day of the month and you have not finished auditing three stores. Your manager asks you to submit partial reports to meet the deadline. What is the most effective action?
sjt.question: What is the most effective action?

options.t: Submit blank reports for the remaining stores to ensure you meet the deadline exactly.
Refuse to submit any reports until all three stores are fully audited, missing the deadline.
Complete the audits for the most critical stores first and clearly state the pending items in the report.
Estimate the findings for the uncompleted stores based on previous months' data.

sjt.title: Data Access
sjt.scenario: A pharmacist from a store asks you to hide a minor policy violation they made because they are a good employee and it was a one-time mistake. What is the most effective action?
sjt.question: What is the most effective action?

options.t: Delete the entry from the audit log to protect the pharmacist's record.
Warn the pharmacist privately and decide whether to report it based on future behavior.
Hide the violation in your notes since it was a minor, one-time error.
Record the violation factually and explain that all findings are reviewed by management.

simulation.title: Audit Day Priorities
simulation.brief: It is a Monday morning. You have a full day of audit tasks for a regional cluster. Rank the following tasks from FIRST (highest priority) to LAST.

items.t: Schedule the follow-up meeting with the store manager to discuss corrective actions.
Conduct the physical stock count and document variance for the first scheduled store.
Draft the preliminary audit report for the first store and note observed process gaps.
Review previous month's unresolved audit findings for critical compliance breaches.
Prepare the audit checklist and verify access to POS and SAP data for the day's scheduled stores.

simulation.rationale: Critical past breaches must be tracked immediately, followed by preparation, then execution of the core audit task, documentation, and finally stakeholder engagement.

caseStudy.title: Expense Reconciliation Mismatch
caseStudy.context: You are auditing the expense records for the Lahore region. Total claimed expenses are PKR 500,000. During verification, you find PKR 50,000 in receipts for fuel that exceed the standard mileage allowance for the declared routes. The regional manager claims the extra fuel was used for emergency deliveries that were not logged in the system. You have no logbook entries to support this claim, but the manager is under pressure to meet sales targets.

questions.q: How would you verify the legitimacy of the extra fuel expenses before finalizing your report?

rubric.point: Suggest checking GPS data or delivery notes from riders.
Recommend interviewing riders or drivers for cross-verification.
Advise comparing fuel consumption against standard benchmarks.

questions.q: The regional manager requests a delay in reporting the discrepancy. How do you handle this request professionally?

rubric.point: State that audit timelines are fixed and cannot be compromised.
Offer to document the manager's explanation as a remark in the report.
Escalate the pressure to your audit supervisor if it hinders objectivity.

questions.q: If the extra expenses are verified as valid but unlogged, what process improvement would you recommend?

rubric.point: Propose a mandatory digital logging system for emergency deliveries.
Suggest a pre-approval workflow for expenses exceeding standard limits.
Recommend regular training for managers on compliance documentation.

voice.q: Why do you want this specific position at DVAGO and what makes you suited to it? (mention the position)
Tell me about a time you had to manage a marketing team to hit a tight sales target during a peak season. What did you do and what was the result?

sjt.title: Compliance vs Sales
sjt.scenario: Your team leader proposes a social media campaign for a prescription drug that claims to 'cure' the condition quickly to boost Q3 sales. Legal has flagged it as a DRAP violation. The campaign is already designed and costs are committed.
sjt.question: What is the most effective action?

options.t: Cancel the campaign entirely and report the team leader to HR
Approve it but reduce the budget to minimize risk
Launch it as is because the sales target is critical
Ask the team to rework the copy to be compliant and delay launch by one week

sjt.title: Underperforming Team Member
sjt.scenario: A digital marketing executive consistently misses KPIs for three months. They claim the tools are outdated. You have data showing their conversion rates are below average compared to peers.
sjt.question: What is the most effective action?

options.t: Ignore it for now as they are new to the role
Transfer them to a different department without discussion
Immediately terminate their contract to save time
Set a clear performance improvement plan with specific targets and weekly reviews

sjt.title: Budget Overrun
sjt.scenario: Mid-month, you realize the digital ad spend is 20% over budget due to high CPMs. The month-end report is due in two days. Sales are still on track.
sjt.question: What is the most effective action?

options.t: Hide the variance in the report to avoid questions
Ask finance to increase the budget limit immediately
Pause low-performing ads, reallocate budget to top performers, and document the variance
Blame the agency for high costs and stop all ads

sjt.title: Cross-Department Conflict
sjt.scenario: The Store Operations Manager complains that your marketing team's 'Flash Sale' caused stockouts at 10 stores, leading to customer complaints. They want you to stop all promotions immediately.
sjt.question: What is the most effective action?

options.t: Agree to stop all promotions to appease the Operations Manager
Tell them marketing is not responsible for inventory management
Escalate to the CEO immediately to get a ruling
Meet with Operations to align on stock availability before launching future promos and apologize for the oversight

simulation.title: Monday Morning Priorities
simulation.brief: It is 9:00 AM on a Monday. You have five urgent tasks on your desk. Rank them from FIRST to LAST based on business impact and urgency.

items.t: Update the monthly budget forecast in Excel for the finance meeting
Approve the media plan for the upcoming Eid campaign to ensure vendor lead time
Review the previous week's sales data to identify any sudden drops in key categories
Draft a response to a customer complaint about a misleading ad on social media
Hold a 15-minute huddle with your team to assign this week's campaign tasks

simulation.rationale: Data review informs immediate adjustments, team alignment ensures execution, vendor approval prevents delays, customer issues need timely but not instant response, and budget updates are routine.

caseStudy.title: Q4 Campaign ROI
caseStudy.context: It is November. The Q4 sales target for DVAGO Pharmacy stores is PKR 50 million. Current run-rate is PKR 40 million. You have a remaining marketing budget of PKR 2 million. Your team proposes a heavy discount campaign (20% off) on top 10 SKUs. However, the Gross Margin on these SKUs will drop by 15%. Competitors are also running similar promotions.

questions.q: Should you approve the 20% discount campaign? Justify your decision using financial and strategic reasoning.

rubric.point: Analyzes impact on Gross Margin
Considers competitive response
Proposes an alternative strategy
Calculates or estimates ROI

questions.q: How would you communicate this strategy to the Store Managers who are already struggling with stock issues?

rubric.point: Uses clear, empathetic communication
Provides specific support or resources
Aligns with store goals
Sets expectations for feedback

questions.q: If the campaign underperforms after two weeks, what is your immediate action plan to recover the target?

rubric.point: Identifies root cause quickly
Pivots strategy or channels
Engages team for solutions
Manages senior management expectations
